<p>In the first days when you hold your baby in your arms, looking into their eyes, you often think: <em>"I wonder if they see me? Do they recognize me?"</em> Although babies' eyes are open from birth, their vision is not as fully developed as other sense organs (such as hearing and smell). The visual system undergoes a gradual development process that lasts for months or even years.</p><p>So, how does this miraculous process happen, from those first days when your baby sees the world as a "blur" to the months when they discover the world in all its colors? Let’s take a month-by-month look at the world through your baby's eyes.</p><h2>Newborn period (0-1 month): Just you and a black-and-white world</h2><p>In the first moments after birth, a baby's retina and the vision center of the brain are not yet fully mature. Their world is quite blurry, and they are very sensitive to light.</p><ul><li><p><strong>Focus distance:</strong> A newborn baby can see relatively clearly at a distance of only <strong>20-30 cm</strong>. Miraculously, this is the distance between a mother's face and the baby's eyes while breastfeeding! Nature created this distance so that the baby can see the thing they need most—their mother.</p></li><li><p><strong>Colors:</strong> In the first weeks, babies cannot distinguish colors. They see the world in shades of black, white, and gray. That is why high-contrast toys or cards (black-and-white checkered or striped) shown to them in the first months attract their visual attention more.</p></li></ul><h2>2-3 months: Awakening of colors and first tracking</h2><p>From the second month, your baby's world begins to become a bit clearer and more colorful.</p><ul><li><p><strong>Discovery of colors:</strong> Color receptors in the eye (cones) begin to develop rapidly. Babies usually start to distinguish the color <strong>red</strong> first, followed by green, yellow, and blue. However, they still cannot distinguish between similar tones (for example, orange and red).</p></li><li><p><strong>Eye tracking:</strong> Your baby can now track moving objects with their eyes. If you slowly move a colored toy from right to left in front of their eyes, you will see their eyes, and sometimes their head, move along with the toy.</p></li><li><p><strong>Making eye contact:</strong> During this period, your baby can now look into your eyes for a long time and examine your facial expressions. This is the moment when the emotional bond between you deepens.</p></li></ul><h2>4-6 months: 3D world and eye-hand coordination</h2><p>These months are a period of major leaps in visual development. The baby's visual acuity increases rapidly.</p><ul><li><p><strong>Depth perception (Stereoscopic vision):</strong> Having previously seen the world like a flat screen, the baby now begins to understand the depth of space by focusing both eyes at the same time (3D vision).</p></li><li><p><strong>Grabbing and grasping:</strong> The development of depth perception allows them to calculate how far objects are. As a result, they can reach out and accurately grab a toy. This is the most important stage of <strong>eye-hand coordination</strong>.</p></li><li><p><strong>All colors:</strong> Your baby can now distinguish almost the entire color spectrum, including pastel tones, as clearly as adults.</p></li></ul><h2>7-12 months: Freedom of movement and full clarity</h2><p>In these months, which are the preparation period for crawling and first steps, the visual system becomes the baby's greatest guide.</p><ul><li><p>Crawling incredibly develops both the baby's eye-hand and body coordination. They can now easily see their favorite toy at the other corner of the room, calculate the distance, and move toward it.</p></li><li><p>Their eye color finally stabilizes. By the age of one, a baby's vision reaches almost the same level as an adult's.</p></li></ul><h2>How can you support your baby's visual development?</h2><ul><li><p><strong>First 2 months:</strong> Hang <strong>black-and-white contrast cards</strong> on the side of the crib or the changing table.</p></li><li><p><strong>3-4 months:</strong> Hang colorful rotating mobiles over the crib so they can both discover colors and track them with their eyes.</p></li><li><p><strong>Change their position often:</strong> Regularly change their position in the crib so they can look at different angles in the room. During the day, surround them with different toys on a rug.</p></li></ul><p></p>
